title: Selective Activation of Peripheral Nerve Fibre Groups of Different Diameter by Triangular Shaped Stimulus Pulses

obligation_rationale: This is a human psychophysics/neurophysiology study using perception threshold tracking with ramp pulses of defined durations (1-200 ms) and specific pin/patch electrode geometries, so readers need electrode dimensions, ramp durations, and body site to interpret fiber-type-specific accommodation findings, though exact current amplitudes were adaptively titrated per subject and not fixed/reported as absolute values.

title: Exploring the Role of Electro-Tactile and Kinesthetic Feedback in Telemanipulation Task
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a multimodal (electro-tactile plus kinesthetic) telemanipulation feedback system tested on human participants, but the excerpts provide no explicit electrical stimulation parameters (current, pulse width, rate, electrode size) delivered to users, so readers are owed at minimum the missing stimulus specification to reproduce or assess safety of the electrotactile channel.

title: A portable, programmable, multichannel stimulator with high compliance voltage for noninvasive neural stimulation of motor and sensory nerves in humans
obligation_rationale: Readers need both the device's rated compliance/current envelope (±150V, 6mA, 3 channels) and the actual delivered stimulation parameters (1.2-3mA, 100-300us, 12.5-200Hz across electrocutaneous/transcutaneous/muscle/nerve targets) to reproduce or compare this noninvasive stimulator's validated human use.

title: Biocompatible, High Precision, Wideband, Improved Howland Current Source With Lead-Lag Compensation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems
obligation_rationale: This paper reports a Howland current-source circuit design for EIT with bench/SPICE-verified output impedance (3.3 Mohm up to 200 kHz) and a 1 kOhm test load, but delivers no stimulus to humans, so only device envelope specs (not delivered dose) are owed to readers.

title: Unmyelinated Afferents Constitute a Second System Coding Tactile Stimuli of the Human Hairy Skin
obligation_rationale: This microneurography study delivered brief constant-current electrical pulses (0.1 ms, up to 15 mA) via surface electrodes solely to estimate afferent conduction velocity, so readers need these delivered parameters and electrode geometry rather than any device rating, since the paper's main contribution is characterizing unmyelinated tactile afferent responses to mechanical (not electrotactile) stimuli.

title: Dynamic Impedance Model of the Skin-Electrode Interface for Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current sweep range, pulse duration, electrode sizes, and biphasic waveform used to derive the dynamic Rs/C/Ge/Gp impedance model, plus the stimulator's 110 mA compliance limit that bounded the sweep.

title: A universal model of electrochemical safety limits in vivo for electrophysiological stimulation
obligation_rationale: As a bench/in-vivo-animal electrochemical safety modeling paper with no human stimulation, it owes readers the tested current, pulse-width and impedance envelope used to derive the universal safety-limit equation, not delivered human dosimetry.

title: Design, evaluation and calibration of wearable electrotactile interfaces for enhancing contact information in virtual reality
obligation_rationale: Reports both the custom stimulator's rated envelope (0.1-9 mA, 30-500 us, 1-200 Hz, 32 channels) and the actual delivered calibration ranges/fixed parameters used per participant, essential for readers to replicate the VR electrotactile interface and its psychophysical calibration.

title: Evidence for sparse C-tactile afferent innervation of glabrous human hand skin
obligation_rationale: This microneurography study delivers only mechanical (brush stroke, monofilament, blunt tap) stimuli to characterize C-tactile afferent physiology, not electrical stimulation, so no electrical dose or device envelope parameters apply.

title: Guidelines for Snowballing in Systematic Literature Studies and a Replication in Software Engineering
obligation_rationale: This is a methodology paper on snowballing for systematic literature reviews, unrelated to electrotactile stimulation devices or human stimulation, so it owes no stimulation parameters.

title: Affective tactile comfort: is a specialized sensory system involved?
obligation_rationale: This is a journal club commentary reviewing prior CT-afferent affective touch research (brush stroking, fMRI) rather than a primary study delivering electrotactile stimulation, so no device or delivered-stimulus parameters are owed.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Electrical Stimulation Haptic Feedback in Human-Computer Interaction
obligation_rationale: As a survey aggregating parameter ranges (intensity 0-6 mA, pulse width 0-400 us, frequency 0-300 Hz) across 110 papers rather than delivering stimuli itself, it owes readers only summary ranges and citations to primary sources, not a specific device envelope or delivered-dose record.

title: Wearable Fabric Electrotactile System with Stimulation–Inhibition Electrode Units
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered stimulation envelope (500 Hz, 200 us pulses, 1-4 mA unipolar current via a 3x4 fabric microelectrode array with stimulation-inhibition electrode geometry) to assess how the novel electrode design's current-focusing effect translates into the reported perceptual accuracy and safety outcomes in 30 participants.

title: Leveraging deep single-soma RNA sequencing to explore the neural basis of human somatosensation
obligation_rationale: This paper delivers mechanical, thermal (QST) and brief electrical search stimuli during human microneurography to classify afferent types, so it owes readers the identified fiber types, conduction velocities and stimulus modalities used, but it reports no programmable electrical stimulator envelope since electrical pulses (0.4 ms) were used only to locate/confirm units, not as a parameterized therapeutic stimulus.

title: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy Increases Electrical Stimulation Threshold of Sciatic Nerve: A Prospective Parallel Cohort Study
venue: Diabetes, Metabolic Syndrome and Obesity: Targets and Therapy
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current threshold range, pulse width, and rate used to elicit motor responses via percutaneous nerve stimulation to compare stimulation-threshold findings across diabetic and control cohorts, since no device output envelope (rated max current/compliance) is reported for the clinical nerve stimulator used.

title: Electrotactile Perception Properties and Its Applications: A Review
obligation_rationale: As a review synthesizing perceptual and device parameters across many primary studies (thresholds, waveform, frequency, electrode siting) without delivering stimuli itself, it owes readers accurate attribution of which parameter ranges and device envelopes came from which cited source rather than its own dosimetry.

title: Explore Electrotactile Parametric Properties Using an Electrical Stimulation System
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a custom 6-channel constant-current stimulator (rated up to 5mA at 90V compliance, load-tested to 18k ohm) and reports the actual delivered parameters (PA 0.1-3mA, PW 100-2000us, PF 5-80Hz, 10mm hydrogel electrodes) used in psychophysical threshold and JND experiments on 8 subjects, so readers need both the device envelope and delivered stimulus values to reproduce or compare the sensory results.
